messages:
mason: Kicking off migration window for feature flags -> canonical_ids. Deploybot will start canary in a few minutes. Release notes: https://redwood.example/release/flags-canonical-2025 :eyes:

deploybot: deploybot: starting canary rollout for migration-id: mig-2025-11-03-42 -> 3% traffic to canary (instances: db-mig-canary-01..03). Watch logs with `kubectl -n prod logs -l release=mig-canary`

jen: quick note — traffic-service is still at v2.8 which expects old schema fields. we should either pin traffic-service to v2.7 for this window or pause the canary. spotted during preflight smoke on staging. cc @mason

sam: +1 saw a NPE in staging when I ran the smoke harness earlier. repro steps in #qa-smoke but probably safe to hold canary until traffic-service patch is out.

mason: thanks. can we estimate time to ship a traffic-service patch?

kevin: patch is small but needs canary and a config flag toggle. i can ship a canary in ~30 mins.

mason: ok — propose we PAUSE canary rollout now and instead do a pinned schedule: 1) pause, 2) wait for kevin canary, 3) resume with 1% traffic and stricter rollback triggers. agree? :thinking:

deploybot: deploybot: canary paused by user mason. current canary traffic set to 0%. rollback policy preserved.

jen: agree. recommend rollback triggers: error_rate >= 1.5% over 5m OR p99 latency increase >= 120ms over baseline for 5m. also enable request-sampling for malformed payloads to catch schema-related errors.

sam: +1 to both. add loggrep alert for "KeyError|NPE|schema mismatch" to make detection fast.

mason: i'll update release notes with the hold and plan. adding a short blurb: "Canary paused due to downstream version mismatch; resume after traffic-service v2.9 canary and validation" — link will be updated once kevin posts canary link.

kevin: starting traffic-service v2.9 canary build now. i'll post the canary url when ready. ETA ~28m.

oncall-bot: alert: deploy window heartbeat check passed. no related incidents open. remember to tag SLO watch owners: @sre and @eng-platform.

mason: operational decision: do not run the big backfill during this hold. backfill will be staged after traffic-service v2.9 full rollout. @kevin please coordinate a 1h quiet window after your canary completes for backfill run.

kevin: noted. i'll target next quiet slot and update calendar.

deploybot: deploybot: pending resume-approval. resume command requires two approvers from list [mason, jen, sam, kevin].

jen: i'll be one approver for resume if canary metrics look good.

sam: i'll second the approval once I validate smoke-run on staging and one canary minute in prod.

mason: action items: kevin -> push traffic-service canary (ETA 28m). sam -> run targeted smoke and loggrep rules. jen -> prep resumed release notes and rollback-policy snippet. i'll hold resume approval until SLOs stable.

kevin: posted canary URL: https://canary-logs.redwood.example/traffic-v2-9/12345 — canary is at 2 instances.

sam: running smoke now, will paste a quick summary in 10m.

(10 minutes pass)

sam: smoke looks clean on staging. prod canary 2 instances show no schema exceptions in last 5m. p95 latency +30ms, error_rate 0.2%.

jen: metrics look good. I approve resume pending 1% initial traffic and the strict rollback triggers.

mason: i approve. resume at 1% for 10m, then 3% for 20m if stable, then continue rollout. deploybot, please resume with plan.

deploybot: deploybot: resume accepted by mason,jen. executing: set canary traffic=1% -> verify 10m -> auto-increase path configured. rollback-if: error_rate>=1.5% over 5m OR p99>=120ms.

kevin: will be watching logs and will hotfix immediately if anything shows.

mason: closing notes: update release notes with canary hold & patch info, and include rollback thresholds. good communication — nice catch, jen. :tada:

oncall-bot: reminder: open incident channel if any of the rollback triggers fire automatically.
